extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the content, formalities, admissibility, and sufficiency of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (and related 1.132) to antedate references and traverse rejections in patent prosecution. Covers who may sign, required facts and exhibits, timing, geographic limitations, and examiner review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species versus embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: References or activities which disclose one or more embodiments of a single claimed invention, as opposed to species of a claimed genus, can be overcome by filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit showing prior completion of a single embodiment of the invention, whether it is the same or a different embodiment from that disclosed in the reference or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and cases (In re Fong, In re Defano) show that when a reference discloses different embodiments (e.g., same inventive concept with different detergents), an affidavit proving prior completion of one embodiment may antedate the reference because the reference is of embodiments rather than species of a genus.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reference discloses a claimed genus (species proof may suffice only in predictable arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reference or activity discloses the claimed genus, a showing of completion of a single species within the genus is sufficient to antedate the reference under 37 CFR 1.131 in general; however, when predictability is in question, a showing of one or a few species generally is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test is whether the species completed by applicant provided an adequate basis for inferring that the invention has generic applicability. The number of species needed depends on genus size and predictability (e.g., small genus such as halogens may need reduction to practice of 2–3 species; large genera require more). See In re Shokal, Mantell, Rainer, Clarke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make the affidavit or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may be made by: (A) all the inventors of the subject matter claimed; (B) less than all named inventors if it is shown the signer(s) invented the subject matter of the claim(s) under rejection; (C) the 37 CFR 1.47 applicant or legal representative where a 1.47 petition was granted or application accepted under 1.42/1.43; (D) the assignee or other party in interest when it is not possible to produce the inventor's affidavit/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fewer than all joint inventors sign, the affidavit must show completion of the invention by all joint inventors of the subject matter. If a joint inventor is deceased, refuses, or unavailable, remaining inventors' signatures may suffice. See Ex parte Foster, In re Carlson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of declarations (per 37 CFR 1.68)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration may be used instead of an affidavit. The declaration must include an acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and may jeopardize the application; declarant must state that statements of the declarant's own knowledge are true and statements made on information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 604.06 for additional formal requirements. Declarations must contain the statutory acknowledgment and appropriate wording distinguishing knowledge vs information/belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration ineffective to overcome U.S. patent or application publication claiming same invention within statutory time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. patent or application publication claims the same invention and its publication date (or issue date) is less than one year prior to presentation of claims to that invention in the application being examined, the applicant's remedy, if any, is by interference (37 CFR 41.202) rather than by 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication/issue is more than one year prior, other statutory provisions like 35 U.S.C. 135(b) may apply to make a rejection. Examiners should note such timing facts in Office actions and use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 23.14, 23.14.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit ineffective when there is no patentable distinction between claims (same patentable invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit is ineffective to overcome a U.S. patent or patent application publication not only when there is verbatim correspondence between claims but also where there is no patentable distinction between the respective claims (i.e., the application and reference claim the 'same patentable invention').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference rules (37 CFR 41.203(a)) define 'same patentable invention'; an applicant cannot use 1.131 to avoid an interference and obtain two patents to the same invention. Where common ownership and non-patentable-distinct claims exist, other tools (e.g., terminal disclaimer, 1.130 affidavits) may be applicable for 35 U.S.C. 103 situations. See In re Clark, In re Hidy, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential requirement: FACTS, not conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential thing to be shown under 37 CFR 1.131 is priority of invention by satisfactory evidence of FACTS; conclusions or general allegations without supporting facts are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/declaration should allege specific facts and refer to exhibits showing those facts. General assertions (e.g., 'invention was completed prior to reference') or conclusory statements without factual support will not satisfy 1.131. Cases: Ex parte Saunders, In re Harry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible documentary evidence/exhibits to support affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence in the form of exhibits may accompany the affidavit or declaration; examples include attached sketches, blueprints, photographs, reproductions of notebook entries, models, supporting statements by witnesses, testimony from an interference, and disclosure documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exhibit relied upon should be specifically referred to in the affidavit/declaration, stating what it is relied upon to show. When relying on interference testimony, applicant must point out which parts are relied upon. Exhibits and models must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered in the application file. See Ex parte Ovshinsky, Ex parte Homan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits requirement: originals or photocopies must accompany or absence explained
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131(b) requires that original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or their absence be satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sketches or models were made and lost, reproduce and furnish reproductions and describe them; if verbal disclosures are relied on, state as nearly as possible the language used. Examiners must consider the affidavit/declaration and all accompanying exhibits/records/notes in their entirety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/exhibit specificity: explain which facts/data are relied on
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit or declaration and exhibits must clearly explain which facts or data applicant is relying on to show completion of the invention prior to the particular date; vague and general statements about what exhibits describe are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must give a clear explanation of exhibits pointing out exactly what facts are established and relied on. Missing limitations in exhibits need not be in every exhibit provided those limitations are supported by the declaration itself. See In re Borkowski, In re Harry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of dates and handling removed/blocked dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dates of the exhibits have been removed or blocked off, dates can be accounted for in the body of the oath or declaration; applicants may allege acts occurred prior to a specified date if they do not wish to give actual dates, but actual dates of acts relied on to establish diligence must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some date flexibility exists for concealing exact dates, diligence allegations require actual dates for the acts relied upon to show continuous activity where diligence is at issue. See MPEP § 715.07(a) for diligence requirement details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ways to show prior invention under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing of facts must be sufficient to show: (A) actual reduction to practice of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference; or (B) conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to a subsequent actual reduction to practice; or (C) conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to the filing date of the application (constructive reduction to practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception alone confers no rights unless followed by reasonable diligence in achieving reduction to practice or filing. Clarifies constructive reduction to practice via filing. See automatic weighing machine case and Mergenthaler v. Scudder for conception standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception and reduction to practice standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception is the mental part of the inventive act and must be capable of proof (e.g., drawings, full disclosure); reduction to practice generally requires showing the apparatus existed and worked for its intended purpose, though for very simple devices mere construction may suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs with articles and technical reports may be sufficient to show reduction to practice for some devices. Proof of utility may be required in 1.131 practice only if the reference discloses a utility; whether test results are needed depends on case facts. See In re Asahi/America, In re Blake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between interference practice and 37 CFR 1.131 practice
rubrics_metrics.description: While terms like 'conception,' 'reasonable diligence,' and 'reduction to practice' are similar in both contexts, the 1.131 practice is not controlled strictly by interference law; e.g., averments in a 1.131 affidavit do not require corroboration and the proof-of-utility standard may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of a 1.131 affidavit is to antedate a reference, not necessarily to demonstrate prior invention in the interference sense. Courts recognize parallels for convenience but not necessity. See In re Eickmeyer, In re Borkowski, Ex parte Hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence requirement and critical diligence period
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligence need not be considered unless conception prior to the effective date is clearly established. Diligence is judged on the particular facts; an inventor is either diligent at a given time or not, but inactivity can be excused if a factual explanation is provided. The critical diligence period begins just prior to the effective date of the reference and ends with reduction to practice (actual or constructive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lapse of time between completion/reduction to practice and filing is not relevant to 1.131. Form paragraph 7.62 may be used to respond when diligence is lacking. See Christie v. Seybold, In re Nelson, MPEP § 2138.06 for detailed discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interference testimony in lieu of affidavit sometimes permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: In place of an affidavit or declaration, testimony of the applicant in an interference may sometimes be used to antedate a reference in lieu of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration, provided the parts of the testimony relied upon are pointed out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must identify which portions of interference testimony form the basis of priority over the reference; examiners are not expected to search entire interference records. See Ex parte Bowyer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts relied upon must have been carried out in the U.S. or NAFTA/WTO member country
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 104 limits establishment of a date of invention by reference to knowledge or use or other activity in a foreign country except where that country is a NAFTA country or a WTO member country (with effective dates). The 1.131 affidavit/declaration must allege that acts relied upon were carried out in the U.S. or in a NAFTA/WTO member country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective dates: NAFTA country dates on/after Dec 8, 1993; WTO member countries (other than NAFTA) on/after Jan 1, 1996. Acts before those effective dates may not establish completion dates under 1.131 for those countries. See statutory text and MPEP discussion of 35 U.S.C. 104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of exhibits (compliance with 37 CFR 1.91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits filed as part of a 1.131 affidavit/declaration must comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into the application file; exhibits that do not comply may be disposed of or returned to applicant at the Office's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.03(a) for further guidance on exhibit handling and entry into the file. Examiners should note noncompliant exhibits and take appropriate disposition actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency review by primary examiner and review/redress channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of sufficiency of affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 should be reviewed and decided by a primary examiner. Review of formal sufficiency and propriety is by petition to Technology Center Directors; review on the merits is by appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to enter an affidavit as untimely is reviewed by petition (not appeal). If applicant disagrees with sufficiency determinations, remedy is by appeal from a continued rejection. See MPEP § 715.08 and § 2138.04–.06 for appeals and interference practice references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonable presentation (timeliness) of affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 must be timely presented; they are considered timely if submitted: (A) prior to a final rejection; (B) before appeal in an application not having a final rejection; (C) after final rejection but before or on same date of filing an appeal upon showing of good and sufficient reasons; or (D) after prosecution is closed if filed with a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) or certain continuation filings in design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All admitted affidavits/declarations are acknowledged and commented upon by the examiner in the next Office action. For affidavits filed after appeal, see 37 CFR 41.33(d) and related MPEP sections. Refusal to enter for untimeliness is by petition. See Form paragraphs guidance for noting timeliness/untimeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review for prior public use/on sale statutory bars and best mode concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must determine whether affidavits/declarations and accompanying evidence show the claimed invention was in public use or on sale in this country more than one year prior to the effective filing date (which would constitute a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)); where 1.131 evidence relies on an embodiment not disclosed in the application, the examiner must consider the best mode requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an affidavit overcomes a reference-based rejection, prior public use/on-sale activities cannot be overcome via 1.131. A best mode rejection should not be made unless the record, taken as a whole, establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that the specification fails to set forth the best mode. See MPEP §§ 2133.03 and 2165–2165.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits/declarations traversing rejections must be responsive and sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected or objected to, evidence to traverse the rejection on a basis not otherwise provided for must be by oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132. The primary examiner is responsible to personally review and decide whether a 1.132 affidavit/declaration is responsive to the rejection and presents sufficient facts to overcome it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is the catch-all for affidavit evidence not covered by other specific rules. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 7.65, 7.66 and 7.66.01–.05) to comment on sufficiency or insufficiency. Examiners should ensure the affidavit specifically addresses the rejection being traversed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph guidance for noting effectiveness or insufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.65 may be used when a 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit/declaration is sufficient to overcome a rejection; form paragraph 7.66 (and subparagraphs) should be used when the affidavit/declaration is insufficient to overcome the rejection, with instructions on inserting filing date, affected claims, and the rejection being overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph templates give exact wording and examiner notes for Office actions (e.g., what to insert in each bracket). Use these to ensure consistent Office action language when admitting or refusing affidavits under 1.132/1.131.
